_comment: Bought parts. 'published' values are quoted from the maker's page at 'source'. 'assumed' values are not published by the maker; each carries the reason it was chosen. Lengths in mm, masses in g.

height_is_case_only.why: the page gives one height; taken as the case without the output spline

shaft_from_end_mm.why: half the case width, as on standard-size servos; not published

ear_overhang_mm.why: typical mounting ear of a standard-size servo; not published

ear_bottom_height_mm.why: about 0.68 of the case height; not published

horn_radius_mm.why: round horn of about 21 mm; the kit's horn is not dimensioned by the maker

horn_face_above_case_mm.why: case top to the outer face of the horn, where the printed blank sits; not published

stall_current_a.why: the maker publishes no stall current; typical for an analog servo of this torque at 5 V

armature_kgm2.why: reflected rotor inertia for the simulation; not published

height_is_case_only.why: the page gives one height; taken as the case without the output spline

shaft_from_end_mm.why: half the case width; not published

ear_overhang_mm.why: typical mounting ear of a mini servo; not published

ear_bottom_height_mm.why: about 0.68 of the case height; not published

horn_radius_mm.why: round horn of about 18 mm; not dimensioned by the maker

horn_face_above_case_mm.why: case top to the outer face of the horn; not published

stall_current_a.why: the maker publishes no stall current; typical for a mini analog servo at 5 V

armature_kgm2.why: reflected rotor inertia for the simulation; not published

supply.note: The Braccio shield feeds the servos from the kit's regulated 5 V supply. The maker rates the servos at 4.8 V and 6.0 V only, so the 4.8 V torque and speed are used.

pcb_thickness_mm.why: standard board thickness; not in the datasheet text

mass_g.why: the datasheet gives no mass; estimate for a populated UNO-format board

spacer_mm.why: insulating spacers the design README asks for; must exceed the 2 mm bottom-side parts

mass_g.why: not published; estimate for the shield with headers and jack

pcb_gap_mm.why: stacking header pitch between board and shield; not published

stack_height_mm.why: top of the servo plugs above the UNO Q board top; not published

esp32cam.name: AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM
esp32cam.source_note: AI-Thinker 'ESP32-CAM Wi-Fi+BT SoC Module V1.0' specification, read from a mirror; docs.ai-thinker.com did not serve the page.

published.connector: none; 2 x 8 pin headers (5V, GND, U0R, U0T, IO0 for power and flashing)

lens_fov_deg.note: 65 to 68 degrees is quoted for the stock OV2640 module; no source says whether diagonal or horizontal

pcb_thickness_mm.why: not published; the snap lips are spaced for 1.6 mm plus 0.3 mm, a thinner board sits loose by the difference

lens_centre_above_lower_edge_mm.why: the camera lies over the card slot at the antenna end, about 9 mm from that edge; not dimensioned by the maker, tolerance 3 mm

lens_front_above_board_mm.why: OV2640 module height on the card slot; not published, tolerance 1.5 mm

lens_diameter_mm.why: module body about 8 mm square; not published

esp_eye.name: Espressif ESP-EYE V2.1
esp_eye.source_note: Espressif's guide names the parts (OV2640 camera, Micro-USB, BOOT and RST buttons on the camera face, a side function button, microphone, 3D antenna) and gives no dimensions. Positions were scaled from its annotated photograph esp-eye_callout.png.

published.connector: Micro-USB on the back face at the lower short edge; powers the board
published.mounting_hole_note: one hole of about 2.3 mm in a corner at the antenna end; one hole cannot locate the board, so it is held by its edges

lens_fov_deg.note: Espressif's figure for the OV2640 on the ESP32-S3-EYE; none is given for the ESP-EYE

lens_centre_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from Espressif's photograph: 9 mm from the antenna end, centred; tolerance 1 mm

lens_diameter_mm.why: module body about 7.7 mm square in the photograph

boot_and_reset_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the photograph: on the camera face, 1.6 mm from each long edge; tolerance 1 mm

side_button_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the photograph: 7 to 11.5 mm, on the long edge at the robot's right; tolerance 1 mm

microphone_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the photograph: camera face, centred, at the USB end

esp32_s3_eye.name: Espressif ESP32-S3-EYE v2.2
esp32_s3_eye.source_note: Espressif's dimension drawings of the main board and its getting-started guide (https://github.com/espressif/esp-who/blob/master/docs/en/get-started/ESP32-S3-EYE_Getting_Started_Guide.md).

published.mounting_hole_note: two holes of about 3 mm in the corners at the antenna end; not used, the antenna end is left open
published.connector: Micro-USB on the back face at the lower short edge

mass_g.why: not published; estimate with the LCD sub board, tolerance 8 g

lens_centre_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the drawing: 10.6 mm from the antenna end, centred; tolerance 0.5 mm

lens_diameter_mm.why: module body scaled from the drawing

stack_thickness.why: the drawings are flat; where the LCD sub board's headers sit along the long edges is not known, so the lip and ledge positions of this preset are the least certain of the three

clear_cone_half_angle_deg.why: covers 66.5 degrees whether that figure is the diagonal or the horizontal field of a 4:3 sensor (39.3 degrees to the corner in the second case)

material.why: the design README names no material

density_g_cm3.why: typical PLA filament data sheet value; PETG is about 1.27

solid_fraction.why: 4 mm plates with two perimeters and 0.8 mm skins at 20 percent infill are mostly shell

screwdriver_radius_mm.why: shank of a small cross-head driver for the horn screw

screwdriver_length_mm.why: free length needed in front of the access hole
